units.translation: you would address them as divided, not as friends
everything creeping up to me is fearful
to whom I came with harmless company
you came as a suppliant, pure and harmless to the house
revere, pray, flatter the ruler always
to the gods later, lady, I will pray

The old scholiast: αἱ ἔμφωνοι [the vocal ones], to which the more recent scholiast adds αἱ προσαγορεύουσαι καὶ μαντευό-μεναι δρύες [the oaks that address and prophesy], i.e. oaks that addressed each person who came to them, pouring forth oracles, as H. Stephanus explains. Seneca called them prophetic oaks in Hercules Oetaeus 1474.
the oaks that address and prophesy
to have come, to be present
to have come, to be present
προσήκει [it is fitting] it is proper, it is seemly
where Meineke in Philologus vol. 20 p. 72 conjectured προσήκον [being fitting]
it is not fitting for you to say this concern
for they were enemies to whom it was fitting to mourn with hair
he calls the god, not fitting to stand by in laments
if I happen to speak to those who are masters and relatives
unless καρδίᾳ [with the heart] is to be written with Casaubon
and the islands along the sea-washed headland, sitting near this land
they sing a hymn, sitting near the house
an arrow sitting near the heart
before, said of time, or earlier
and, where the meter demands, πρόσθε [before], which the Ionians also use in prose, about which I have spoken in the Thesaurus vol. 6 p. 1926. In a local sense
the prow in front, looking at the road with its eyes
there is an island before the region of Salamis
and before this man a wondrous ambush sleeps
only before have I seen another
I have made the fiery signs clear, which before were white spots
whom Marathon before destroyed of the barbarians
the fate will destroy the cattle before, the people-nourishing ones
I will not turn aside the former track of my mind
as before, being well-disposed to me
of the house not as before being excellently managed
if he comes here before me
for well may there be an addition to those who appear well
thus Auratus for Λοξίου [of Loxias]. προσθί-γων Μ [touching, M]
Loxias, touching you, will make you free from these troubles
Meineke conjectured for προσίξεται [will approach] Choephori 1033.
Choephori 321: and the graces are likewise called a glorious lament for the Atreidae before the house.
